simple.meaning: נְתַן (nᵉthan) is a Hebrew action word meaning “give.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 4:13. The surrounding contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְתַן (H5415) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נְתַן (nᵉthan) / H5415 is traced through Ezra 4:13, Ezra 7:20, Daniel 2:16, Daniel 4:14 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the kings.
Whatever more will be needed for the house of your God, which you may have occasion to give, give it out of the king’s treasure house.

Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
He cried aloud, and said this, ‘Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches! Shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit! Let the animals get away from under it, and the fowls from its branches.
it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
